title: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
abstract: arXiv:2610.00093v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong general capabilities, yet their parameters typically remain fixed after deployment, limiting learning from new interactions. In open-ended environments, this motivates self-evolving agents that continually update reusable state-including model parameters, memories, tool definitions, skills, and workflows-from data, feedback, and accumulated experience. This shift changes the safety problem: once experience becomes reusable state, past events become future causes, and information harmless in one context may later influence decisions with greater persistence, authority, or scope. Self-evolving agent safety therefore asks not only whether a response is aligned or an action authorized, but whether safety properties survive the accumulation, generalization, and cross-context reuse of locally useful experience. translated_title: 自进化智能体的安全性：综述
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）展现出强大的通用能力，但其参数在部署后通常保持固定，限制了从新的交互中学习的能力。在开放式环境中，这催生了自进化智能体——它们持续地从数据、反馈和积累的经验中更新可复用的状态，包括模型参数、记忆、工具定义、技能和工作流。这一转变改变了安全性问题的本质：一旦经验成为可复用的状态，过去的事件就会成为未来的原因，在某一情境中无害的信息日后可能以更强的持久性、权威性或更大的影响范围来左右决策。因此，自进化智能体的安全性问题不仅要追问某次响应是否对齐、某个行动是否获得授权，更要追问安全属性能否在局部有用经验的积累、泛化和跨情境复用过程中得以存续。我们提出了SAVER，一个以状态转移为中心的框架，其中“基底”定位可复用的
tldr: 这篇综述提出SAVER框架，系统研究自进化智能体的安全问题，指出当经验成为可复用状态后，安全属性必须在经验的积累、泛化与跨情境复用中持续存续，从而将安全研究从单次响应对齐扩展到持续演化视角。
en_tdlr: This survey introduces SAVER, a transition-centered framework for safety in self-evolving agents, arguing that safety properties must survive the accumulation, generalization, and cross-context reuse of locally useful experience as agents continually update reusable state such as parameters, memories, tools, skills, and workflows.
